- Keep stdlib only. Keep existing unit tests passing.

"""TableSync: a tiny restaurant ops board (prep list, 86 list, shift notes).
Standard library only. Run: python3 app.py  -> http://localhost:8000
Per-shift PIN login: owner sets a PIN, cooks log in with it on their phone.

STATE = {"prep": [], "eighty_six": [], "notes": []}
SHIFT = {"pin": None}
TOKENS = set()

def add(section, text):
    if section not in STATE or not text.strip():
        return False
    STATE[section].append(text.strip())
    return True

def set_shift_pin(pin):
    pin = str(pin)
    if not pin.isdigit() or not 4 <= len(pin) <= 6:
        return False
    SHIFT["pin"] = pin
    TOKENS.clear()  # new shift PIN invalidates old tokens
    return True

def login(pin):
    if SHIFT["pin"] is None or str(pin) != SHIFT["pin"]:
        return None
    token = secrets.token_hex(16)
    TOKENS.add(token)
    return token

# TableSync
A simple shared ops board for small restaurant kitchens: prep list, 86 list (items out of stock), and shift notes.
Built with Python standard library only. Includes a JSON API (GET /api/state, POST {section,text}) and unit tests.

Run: `python3 app.py` then open http://localhost:8000
Test: `python3 test_app.py`

Next: mobile-friendly UI, login per shift, pilot with a local restaurant.
